repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaacEFVpyQ6C5mcRQs

Decision analysis · 2026-11-25T23:48Z · decision thread for zone o5-U (inbox 7177760930)

## 维护者速读

- 问题：下拉选项没登记颜色时，列表、看板、筛选里的标签仍被平台按值自动上色（查表或哈希）。HotCRM 线索列表里「来源」「需求类型」没配颜色，却一个粉一个紫，用户以为颜色有含义，其实没有；偶尔还会配反（之前 info 被配成橙色警报）。
- 选项：A 全部去掉自动配色：没登记颜色就是中性灰，登记了才有色，甘特图和日历同规则，不加开关，1 个前端 PR 加 1 个服务端小 PR 给系统通知的严重度登记颜色；B 只去掉哈希、保留按值查表，info 蓝 open 蓝继续；C 都保留，加一个字段级开关让应用关掉；D 维持现状，HotCRM 给 280 个选项逐个写灰色。
- 推荐 A：标签颜色只应表达作者登记的含义；平台替作者猜颜色，猜对是运气，猜错是误导。
- 不定会怎样：HotCRM 等应用继续看到无含义的彩色标签，或者为了关掉它在元数据里给每个选项写灰色。

## Background

`getBadgeColorClasses(color, val)` (`ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx`) resolves a badge colour in three rungs: the declared option `color` (family or hex, objectui#5141); `SEMANTIC_COLOR_MAP[value]` (92 hard-coded English and Chinese values); `hashToColor(value)` into an 8-colour palette. `getSemanticColorName` and the `appearance: 'dot'` branch repeat rungs 2–3. Callers: grid cells and group rows, kanban, the filter value panel, Gantt bars (rung 3 for a declared `colorField`, plus a status/priority fallback). The calendar has its own hash onto an 8-stop palette (`CalendarView.tsx`). The only declared colour key is `SelectOption.color` ("Color code for badges/charts"); no field or view key turns rungs 2–3 off. HotCRM's maintainer asked on 2026-11-24: 「去掉系统默认的配色功能。」 #27521 row 4 ("info drawn orange") was remedied in PR #27849 by adding `info`/`warning` to the table, pinned by `badge-severity-27521.test.ts`.

## Governing text

- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:403` `color: z.string().optional().describe('Color code for badges/charts')` — the one declared colour; `:472` `kind: 'open'|'won'|'lost'` is the declared lifecycle category (ADR-0085 semantic roles). — `sed -n 403p packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts; sed -n 472p packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`
- ADR-0085 stage-role row names "list badges" as a future reader of `stageField`/`kind` — `grep -n "list badges" docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md`
- `ui/packages/core/src/utils/record-color.ts` (objectui#7243): `colorField` rungs 1 option colour, 2 CSS literal, 3 caller-specific; "if neither exists GanttView paints the platform default blue" — `sed -n 28,38p ui/packages/core/src/utils/record-color.ts`
- Renderer comment on the table: "Semantic color mapping (auto-detect from value text for priority & status fields)" — a heuristic no spec text declares — `sed -n 1547,1551p ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx`
- Prior remedy in conflict: PR #27849 row 4 and pin `ui/packages/fields/src/__tests__/badge-severity-27521.test.ts` ("info is blue and warning is yellow").
- No ADR, NORTH-STAR line or skill rule promises automatic colouring — `grep -rn -i "hashToColor\|SEMANTIC_COLOR_MAP\|automatic colou" docs/adr skills AGENTS.md` → 0.

## Protocol

No spec change. `Metadata-protocol: none`; the renderer's default changes for every app's undeclared options, so the changeset names that reach (minor on `@object-ui/fields` and the plugins).

## Premises (each with a re-check)

1. Three rungs in `getBadgeColorClasses`, repeated in `getSemanticColorName` and the dot branch — `sed -n 1822,1851p ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx; sed -n 1930,1936p ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx`
2. The table holds 92 values in two languages — `sed -n 1551,1665p ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx | grep -cE "^\s*[^/ ]+:\s*'"`
3. Callers outside tests: grid, GroupRow, kanban, FilterValuePanel, gantt, types docblock; calendar hashes on its own — `grep -rln "getBadgeColorClasses\|getSemanticColorName" ui/packages --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v test; grep -n "hash" ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx`
4. Gantt rung 3 paints a declared `colorField` whose options carry no colour from the table/hash, then falls back to status/state/priority/severity — `sed -n 1529,1545p ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx`
5. In-repo examples: 183 select options, 89 with `color`, 94 without (showcase, todo, crm) — a python count over `examples/**/*.ts` of `{ label, value[, color] }` literals
6. `platform-objects` declares `Field.select(['info','warning','critical'])` for `sys_notification.severity` with no colours; it relies on the table today — `grep -rn "Field.select(\['info'" packages/platform-objects/src | grep -v test`
7. #27521 row 4 pin asserts table colours for undeclared `info`/`warning`/`critical` — `sed -n 9,20p ui/packages/fields/src/__tests__/badge-severity-27521.test.ts`

## The question in one sentence

A badge is coloured although its author declared no colour, so readers cannot tell a meant colour from an accidental one, and sometimes the accident says the opposite of the value.

## Options × real cost × workload

| | What | What the person sees | Workload |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Colour iff declared, on every surface. Delete the table, the hash and the calendar's own hash; undeclared ⇒ neutral badge/dot (`bg-muted …`, `DOT_COLOR_MAP.gray`); Gantt keeps `colorField` rungs 1–2 (declared option colour, CSS literal) and otherwise paints the default bar; calendar paints its default event colour; no opt-in switch. Platform objects that rely on the table today (`sys_notification.severity`) declare their colours. The #27521 row-4 pin is rewritten to assert the declared path (ruling supersedes the renderer remedy). | Undeclared options are grey everywhere, light and dark; declared colours unchanged; Notifications keeps severity colours by declaration. In-repo showcase: 94 options turn grey. | domain:ui 1 PR, size S–M (−~130 lines table/hash, 6 call sites, calendar, 2 tests rewritten). Precedent: PR #27849 (+789/−66, 39 files) was a multi-row PR whose row-4 half was ~15 lines. domain:server 1 PR, size S (declare colours on the platform selects that lose theirs; enumerate at claim). |
| B | Delete the hash only; keep the table. | Values the table knows stay coloured (`open` blue in any field, `high` orange whether priority or grade; two languages only); unknown values grey. #27521 row 4 stays as ruled. | domain:ui 1 PR, size S. Half the mechanism stays, with its field-blind guesses. |
| C | Keep both; add a field-level switch (e.g. `autoColor: false`) to turn them off. | Default unchanged; an app opts out per field. | domain:spec + ui, 2 PRs, size M (new declared key, forms, docs, liveness row). A permanent key whose only purpose is to switch off a default nobody declared. |
| D | Status quo; HotCRM writes `color: 'gray'` on ~280 options. | Unchanged; app metadata pays for a platform default. | 0 platform PRs; ~280 metadata edits in the app. |

Business translation: A = a colour on a badge is a statement by the author, as a status colour is in any CRM where the admin sets it per value; B = the platform keeps a half-dictionary of English/Chinese words it thinks it understands; C = a new knob to silence a guess; D = the app pays per option for the platform's habit.

## Four axes (business stance)

- **Real business need (②)** — measured: the HotCRM maintainer's request (2026-11-24); Lead Source "Cold Call" pink, "Website" indigo, "Replacement" orange on the lead list with nothing in metadata saying so; #27521 row 4 was this mechanism misfiring (`info` orange). 280 undeclared options in HotCRM; 94 in the in-repo examples. Nobody has asked for automatic colouring; it is a renderer habit.
- **Long-term fit (①)** — colour is a declaration. Two years out, a badge's colour comes from the option's `color`, and any semantic colouring (won green, lost red) comes from the declared `kind` on the stage field (ADR-0085's "list badges" reader), never from the value string. Mainstream: Salesforce picklists are uncoloured until an admin sets a colour per value (path/kanban); Airtable and Notion store an auto-assigned colour on the option as metadata, editable, not derived at render. A matches declared-colour modelling; B keeps a value-keyed dictionary that is wrong across fields and languages; C adds a key to silence it.
- **AI-error-proofing (③)** — today an AI authoring metadata sees colours appear it never wrote and believes colour "works"; a Spanish or German value gets a hash colour, an English one gets a dictionary colour, and neither is an error anyone sees. With A a missing colour is visibly neutral, so the author declares what they mean; nothing silent remains. The failure mode of A is loud (grey badges), the failure mode of B/C/D is a wrong colour that looks intended.
- **Startup focus (④)** — remove beats declare-and-maintain: A deletes a 92-row two-language table and a palette; C adds a permanent key; D moves the cost into every app. No new gate; `objectstack validate` does not warn on a `colorField` without option colours (a docs line instead).

os-decision-facets
① Long-term fit: colour iff declared; deletes the value-keyed heuristic and leaves semantic colouring to the declared `kind` (ADR-0085) if ever wanted.
② Business pull: HotCRM maintainer request 2026-11-24; misleading colours on Lead Source / Need Type; #27521 row 4 was this mechanism misfiring; 280 undeclared options in HotCRM.
③ AI-error-proofing: undeclared ⇒ visibly neutral instead of a plausible wrong colour; no two-language dictionary that English values pass and others fail.
④ Startup focus: remove 92-row table + hash + calendar hash; no new key (C) and no gate; cost moves out of app metadata (D).
Prior rulings read: badge · colour · color · 27521 · 配色 · hashToColor → 0 hits in coordinator/rulings.md and decisions/待决汇总.md; conflict: PR #27849 row 4 (comment 6513177556 on #27521) adds `info`/`warning` to the table, pinned by `badge-severity-27521.test.ts`; objectui#7243 (record-color.ts) and objectui#5141 (hex) read from code; ADR-0085 stage roles; thread: none.

## Recommendation: A

Self-check: 只看①选 A;②③④ 是否翻转:否。

Confidence gaps: (a) HotCRM's metadata is not in this container; the 280 count and the lead-list colours are the card's reading. (b) The full list of platform selects that rely on the table was not enumerated here (one found: `sys_notification.severity`); the server follow-up enumerates on claim. (c) Dashboard/report chart series colours use `buildOptionColorMap` (`chart-series.ts`), not these helpers; whether charts hash undeclared series colours is not measured here and stays outside this ruling.

Not taken: B keeps a field-blind, two-language guess; C adds a permanent key to silence a default; D makes every app pay per option.

## Answers to the card's three questions (under A)

1. Table and hash both go. The #27521 row-4 remedy moves from the renderer to the declaration: the platform object declares `info`/`warning`/`critical` colours. The pin test is rewritten, not deleted.
2. Gantt `colorField`: rungs 1–2 stay; rung 3 and the status/priority fallback go; a declared `colorField` whose options carry no colours paints the default bar colour. Declaring `colorField` is asking the platform to read the field's colours, not to invent them; the docs say so.
3. No opt-in switch. Declaring colours on options is the only way to get them.

Also under A: the calendar's own hash goes the same way (default event colour), so every surface answers one rule.

## Execution after the ruling (A)

1. Zone o5-U claims #36882 (`domain:ui`, size S–M). The `repo:hotcrm` label on the card names the finder's repo, not the landing repo (the fix is in `ui/**`); the zone asks triage to correct it with an audit comment, or notes it on the claim.
2. UI PR: delete `SEMANTIC_COLOR_MAP`, `BADGE_FALLBACK_PALETTE`, `hashToColor`; `getBadgeColorClasses` declared-else-neutral; `getSemanticColorName` declared-else-`undefined`; dot branch declared-else-gray; Gantt per question 2; calendar default event colour; rewrite `badge-severity-27521.test.ts` and the no-colour cases of `badge-hex-fidelity-5141.test.tsx`; pins for each surface in the card's blast table plus calendar, light and dark. Changeset minor naming the reach. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs:` a line in `skills/objectstack-ui` that colour is declared via `color`.
3. Server follow-up card under #36882 (`domain:server`, size S): declare colours on platform-object selects that rely on the table (enumerate; `sys_notification.severity` is one), landed before or with the UI PR so Setup's Notifications page does not regress.
